title: Rational addition renormalises and negation is an additive inverse
statement: Rat.add returns the reduced representative of a sum (1/6 + 1/3 is 1/2, reached as 9/18), Rat.neg is an involution that moves its argument, and x + (-x) is 0. Negation alone needs no renormalisation, because negating a numerator does not change the magnitude the reducedness field constrains.

evidence.supports: 1/6 + 1/3 is 1/2 and is not 1/3; neg is an involution on 1/2 and does move it; 1/2 + (-1/2) is 0.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib rat_add_renormalises_and_neg_is_an_involution 2>&1 | grep -Ec '^test result: ok\. 1 passed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: Bound to this test by name, with `1 passed` required so an empty filter cannot pass. The `1/2 + (-1/2) = 0` case is the one that matters most: it is the only check here that drives a genuinely NEGATIVE numerator through Rat.normalize's negSucc branch, which the ofNat-only cases never reach.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- Rat is built in the integer environment, whose trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: Rat and its operations are admitted into the same environment as the integer development, so an empty trusted surface bounds their footprints. Environment-wide on purpose: a declaration cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain.
